- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, particularly after recent spikes.
- Underestimate during mid-to-late horizon when true values show upward momentum or mean reversion.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.68 → 82.x) by 2–5% and fail to correct downward.
- Model tends to lag mean reversion by 3–7 days; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per day after peak.
- Avoid overreacting to recent low values; model often underestimates recovery from dips.
- Forecast bias is upward in the first 10 days, then downward in the last 10 days — apply asymmetric correction.
- Use 3-day moving average of true values to smooth out noise and adjust forecast baseline.
